title: DHS bans DeepSeek products across US federal civilian agencies
description: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has ordered all federal civilian agencies to stop using DeepSeek products and remove them from government systems due to security and privacy concerns. The ban includes products from DeepSeek affiliates and third-party services built on DeepSeek technology. Concerns include potential Chinese government access to user data, unencrypted data transmissions, weak encryption, insecure local storage, user fingerprinting, and data sharing with ByteDance. Agencies may request exceptions with justification and risk mitigation plans, subject to CISA approval. The order does not apply to private or consumer use and aims to protect sensitive government data from potential exfiltration to China.
aiSummary: DHS has issued a directive banning the use of DeepSeek products across U.S. federal civilian agencies, citing risks of Chinese government access to infrastructure and sensitive data. The ban extends to affiliates and third-party products using DeepSeek technology. A February 2025 NowSecure report highlighted security vulnerabilities in the DeepSeek iOS app, including unencrypted transmissions, weak encryption, insecure storage, user fingerprinting, and data sharing with ByteDance. Agencies must remove these products or seek exceptions within 60 days. CISA will review exception requests and provide technical assistance if needed. The order is intended to mitigate risks of data exposure and potential malware embedded in DeepSeek models.
aiImpact: The directive addresses risks of unauthorized access to sensitive government information through DeepSeek products, including potential data exfiltration to the Chinese government. Vulnerabilities such as unencrypted data transmission and insecure storage increase the risk of data interception and compromise. The presence of user fingerprinting and data sharing with ByteDance raises privacy concerns. The ban aims to prevent these risks from affecting federal civilian agencies' IT systems, thereby protecting government data confidentiality and integrity.
